messages.subject: Hessian eigenvalue warnings with Student-t model
parts:
Hi,

I have developed a model assuming Gaussian likelihood. I wanted to test this assumption by using Student-t model. However, I am receiving warnings about negative Hessian eigenvalues (printout shown below). I have centred and scaled the modelled variable as well as covariates and the Gaussian model fits ok (I believe) Is there any guidance what I should do/test/check etc.?

Many thanks!

Regards, Gregor

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Hessian eigenvalue warnings with Student-t model
parts:
Hi

yes, the problem is deep. the issue is that student-t is not log-
concave, and the question is what to do if the local hessian for the
log student-t (like for one observation) has the wrong sign. its like
getting variance < 0, so the contribution for the student-t observation
will locally inflate the variance, not reducing it.

its possible to truncate this at 0, meaning that if the hessian has the
wrong sign, set it to zero. you can do this using

control.inla = list(cmin = 0)

where the default value is -Inf which means do nothing. its unclear
what is the better thing to do, beyond the obvious, which comes with a
higher cost.

to be honest, I do not like the student-t anymore ;-)

H

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Hessian eigenvalue warnings with Student-t model
parts:
You can add informative priors to all the model components. This often helps. Check out
>> inla.doc("pc.prec")
and
>> inla.doc("pccor1")

PS. You can of course do a scenario analysis of the T parameter: Fix it, run the model, compare results across fixed T parameters.

Kind regards,
Haakon Bakka
